title: Are we in a sixth mass extinction?
sub: Symposium topic 7 · Ceballos et al. 2015 vs Wiens & Saban 2025
blurb: The Big Five, background vs contemporary extinction rates, extinction debt.
h1: Are we facing a sixth mass extinction?
lede: Group 7's question. Classic: Ceballos et al. (2015), 'Entering the sixth mass extinction'. Recent: Wiens & Saban (2025), 'Questioning the sixth mass extinction'.
six: **Big Five**: periods with ≥75 % species lost: End-Ordovician, Late Devonian, End-Permian, End-Triassic, End-Cretaceous.
**Background extinction rate**: the natural pace from the fossil record, about **2 E/MSY** (extinctions per million species-years).
**Ceballos 2015** defines mass extinction by **rate**: modern rates vastly exceed background, even with conservative data.
**Wiens & Saban 2025** define it by **total loss** (75 %), and total loss so far is very low.
**Extinction debt**: species already committed to extinction by past damage, with a time lag of years to centuries.
Group 7's verdict: the warning is real (rates are high, humans drive them), but by the 75 % definition we are not there yet. Conservation is the window.
must: background vs contemporary rates and the Big Five
foot: Source: Group 7 symposium slides; glossary section 7.

questions.q: Which list gives the Big Five mass extinctions in order?
questions.answer: End-Ordovician, Late Devonian, End-Permian, End-Triassic, End-Cretaceous
wrong: Late Devonian, End-Ordovician, End-Triassic, End-Permian, End-Cretaceous
End-Ordovician, End-Permian, Late Devonian, End-Cretaceous, End-Triassic

questions.q: What share of species is lost in a mass extinction by the classic definition?
What is the background extinction rate used by Ceballos et al.?
questions.e: 0.1–1 E/MSY rounded up to a conservative 2 E/MSY: about 1 extinction per 10,000 species per 100 years.

questions.q: Background extinction rates are inferred from…
questions.answer: The fossil record in geologically normal periods

questions.q: How does Ceballos et al. 2015 define a mass extinction?
questions.answer: By how fast species disappear compared with background rates
wrong: By the total share of species lost
By the number of new species

questions.q: How do Wiens & Saban 2025 define a mass extinction?
wrong: By the number of invasive species
questions.e: By that measure total loss so far remains very low.

questions.q: According to Ceballos, the vertebrate extinctions of the last 100 years would naturally have taken…
questions.e: One of the reasons FOR the sixth mass extinction.

questions.answer: Only species officially listed as extinct
questions.e: Conservative adds extinct in the wild and possibly extinct.

questions.q: Which is a reason AGAINST calling it a sixth mass extinction?
questions.answer: Historical extinctions are heavily biased toward islands
questions.e: Others: total loss still very low; invertebrates omitted.

questions.answer: Future extinctions already committed by past habitat damage
questions.e: There is a time lag between cause and extinction.

questions.q: How long can the time lag in extinction debt be?
questions.e: That lag is a window for restoration.

questions.q: The New Zealand shrub Rhabdothamnus solandri is in extinction debt because…
questions.answer: Several of its bird pollinators went locally extinct around 1870
wrong: Its seeds are eaten by rats
questions.e: It relies on native bird pollinators.
